outcomes.text: Define the terms benevolent, omniscient, omnipotent, monotheistic, judge, eternal, transcendent, immanent, personal and forgiving.
Explain the significance for Christians of these characteristics of God.
Compare how different denominations emphasise these characteristics and interpret sources of authority.
Explain the Trinity as one God in three persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit.
Explain the relationship between Father, Son and Holy Spirit and issues about the nature of God.
Compare different Christian attitudes to God as Trinity.
Explain the concept of God as creator and the role of God the Father in Genesis.
Explain the role of the Spirit in Genesis 1-2 and of the Word in John 1, identifying Jesus as the Word linked to creation.
Explain the role and purpose of human beings and the Fall in Genesis.
Explain issues raised by Genesis, comparing literal and metaphorical understandings.

subtopics.title: The problem of evil and suffering

outcomes.text: Explain concepts of evil and good, natural and moral evil, and the causes of evil.
Explain the Fall as a result of free will and the concept of original sin.
Explain the problem of how an omnipotent, benevolent and righteous God allows evil and suffering.
Explain the terms Messiah, Son of God, Lord and Saviour and their significance and relevance for Christians today.
Explain the role of Jesus' teachings and life as an example, including agape.
Explain the Christian ideal in the Sermon on the Mount.
Define the incarnation, crucifixion, resurrection and ascension.
Explain the beliefs arising from them and their importance for Christian life and worship.
Compare denominational emphases on their significance.
Define salvation, atonement, law, sin, grace and Spirit.
Explain the role of Christ in salvation, including his sacrifice.
Explain forgiveness and repentance, the nature of atonement, and common and divergent beliefs about the need for salvation and Christ's role.
Define resurrection, life after death, heaven and hell.
Describe apocalyptic ideas in the Early Church.
Compare beliefs about the Second Coming (Parousia).
Compare beliefs about death, judgement, purgatory, heaven and hell.
Describe the structure of church services: Anglican Communion, Roman Catholic mass, Quaker meeting, Greek Orthodox and Methodist worship.
Explain the concept and purposes of worship.
Explain the role of liturgical and of informal or charismatic worship.
Explain the role of individual, private and public worship for communities and individuals.
Explain the meaning and role of sacraments.
Explain the role of Baptism and Eucharist in Christian life.
Compare denominational attitudes to Baptism, the Eucharist and which practices count as sacraments.
Explain the concept, importance and impact of prayer, including in worship.
Explain the meaning and use of the Lord's Prayer.
Describe types of prayer: adoration, confession, thanksgiving, supplication, grace, intercession, praying in the spirit, chants and meditation.
Compare set liturgical prayer with informal extempore prayer.
Explain the concept of pilgrimage and its purpose to Lourdes, Jerusalem, Walsingham and Rome, and its impact.
Explain the origin of Christmas and Easter.
Explain the importance of Advent, Christmas, Lent, Holy Week and Easter.
Compare denominational attitudes to pilgrimage and celebrations.

subtopics.title: The role of the church in the local community

outcomes.text: Explain the importance of rites of passage and the rituals that mark them.
Describe how churches support families: Sunday schools, youth clubs, mother and child groups, visiting the elderly and sick.
Compare denominational practices on membership: infant baptism, dedication, believers baptism and confirmation.
Compare denominational attitudes to and practices of marriage and funerals.
Explain the meaning and importance of mission in the modern church and compare denominational attitudes in 21st century Britain.
Explain evangelism, compare attitudes to it and describe evangelism in practice.
Describe the growth of new forms of church and the reasons for it.

subtopics.title: The role of the church in the wider world

outcomes.text: Explain the terms ecumenical and Church, and the purpose of the World Council of Churches.
Describe ecumenical communities such as Taize, Iona, Corrymeela and Churches Together.
Explain persecution of the Church in the 21st century and how it is supported.
Explain the purpose of one Christian aid agency: Christian Aid, Tearfund or Cafod.
Explain the six articles of faith in Sunni Islam and their importance.
Explain the meaning of Usul ad-Din and the five roots in Shi'a Islam: Tawhid, Adl, Nubuwwah, Imamah and Ma'ad.
Explain the Shi'a beliefs about justice and imamate that differ from Sunni Islam.
Compare the views of different Muslim groups on core beliefs.
Explain the importance of the 99 names of Allah, including Tawhid, merciful, omnipotent, benevolent, fair and just, transcendent and immanent.
Explain Tawhid and shirk and their implications for polytheism and Christianity.
Explain how Allah's attributes are shown: creator and judge, concern and intervention, and merciful guidance.
Explain the Shi'a concept of Imamate and its relation to Tawhid.
Explain the role of prophets: Adam, Ibrahim, Isma'il, Musa, Dawud and Isa.
Explain Muhammad as seal of the prophets, his background and personal qualities.
Explain Risalah as Allah's way of communicating with humans.
Explain the twelve Imams and their infallibility in Shi'a Islam.
Explain Islam as the original religion dating back to Adam.
Describe the Scrolls, Injil, Tawrat and Zabur revealed to earlier messengers and how the original belief became distorted.
Explain the Qur'an as the final undistorted message and compare Muslim attitudes to books and ancient texts.
Explain the roles of Jibril, Izra'il, Mika'il and Israfil.
Describe angels as Allah's first creation: immortal, sinless and without free will, and as communicators between Allah and humans.
Explain how belief in recording angels may affect daily behaviour.
Explain predestination (al-Qadr) as a divine masterplan and the idea of sifat.
Explain human freedom and the Day of Judgement, including the book of life.
Compare Sunni and Shi'a views on human freedom: Mu'tazilite and Al-Ashari.
Explain Akhirah and life as preparation for the life to come.
Explain human responsibility and accountability, and stewardship.
Describe Barzakh, heaven (al-Jannah) and hell (Jahannam), and literal and metaphorical interpretations.
Discuss the issue of martyrdom.
Explain Islam as a way of life in total submission to Allah.
Explain the Five Pillars for Sunni Muslims: Shahadah, Salat, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj, and the house and pillars analogy.
Explain the Ten Obligatory Acts for Shi'a Muslims, including Khums, Jihad, Amr-bil-Maroof, Nahi Anil Munkar, Tawalla and Tabarra.
Explain how and why Muslims pray: ablution, times, direction, movements and recitations, at home and in the mosque.
Explain worship as a reminder of Shirk and Tawhid, and the purpose of congregational prayer and the khutba.
Explain the place of the Shahadah in Muslim practice and as the only non-action pillar.
Explain Salah as direct communication with Allah, Jummah attendance, wudu, niyyah, qibla and raka't.
Explain du'a and its importance, and the difference between du'a and salah.
Explain the importance, obligation and origins of Hajj and how and why it is performed.
Explain the exceptions to Hajj, Ihram regulations and the significance of the rituals.
Define Zakah and Khums and explain the origins, purpose and benefits of giving alms.
Explain the Muslim attitude to wealth as given by Allah and to be shared, and sadaqah as voluntary alms.
Explain Nisab (2.5%), how alms are distributed, and how Khums and Zakah differ and are apportioned.
Explain the role of fasting in Ramadan: origins, devotion to Allah, duties and benefits to individuals and the Ummah.
Describe exemptions from fasting, the Night of Power and Ramadan as the month the Qur'an was sent down.
Compare experiences of Sawm in Muslim and non-Muslim countries.
Explain the origin and meaning of Eid-ul-Adha, Eid-ul-Fitr, Eid-ul-Ghadeer and Ashura.
Explain their importance for different groups of Muslims.
Discuss issues in celebrating festivals in Muslim and non-Muslim countries.
Explain Greater Jihad and Lesser Jihad and the precedence of Greater over Lesser.
Explain conditions for declaring and conducting Lesser Jihad and the concepts of Munkar and Ma'ruf.
Compare Muslim views on if and when holy war should be waged.
Explain G-d as One, Creator, Law-Giver, Judge and Eternal.
Explain the significance for Jews of G-d as all-powerful, all-good, all-knowing, everywhere, beyond time and space, concerned, intervening, transcendent and immanent.
Discuss the problem of evil and suffering.
Compare Jewish views on the Last Day and G-d's judgement on Rosh Hashanah.
Explain the meaning, origins and significance of Shekinah.
Explain the association of Shekinah with feminine aspects of G-d and the Sefirot.
Discuss the relationship between G-d and the prophets.
Compare Jewish views of Shekinah as synonymous with G-d or as G-d dwelling on Earth.
Explain the concept of Covenant and the significance of the Sinai Covenant and Ten Commandments.
Explain the role of Moses.
Explain G-d's promises to the Israelites and their significance for modern Judaism.
Explain the meaning, concept and origins of the term Messiah and the role of Elijah.
Explain the importance of the Messiah in Jewish history and the characteristics of the Messiah.
Explain the Messianic Age as an era of global peace and compare Jewish views of the Messiah and his coming.
Explain the Promised Land: to whom it was promised, and in return for what.
Explain the Covenant with Abraham and Abraham's importance.
Compare Jewish groups' attitudes to the Promised Land and the State of Israel.
Explain the meaning and significance of Mitzvot, including positive (aseh) and negative (ta'ashe) commandments.
Explain Divine Providence and the relationship between free will and the Mitzvot.
Explain Pikuach Nefesh as taking precedence over other commandments.
Compare emphasis on interpersonal relationships as the principle behind some Mitzvot.
Explain ethical and ritual Mitzvot and how they build relationships between man and G-d and between people.
Explain the difference between them and the significance of ethical Mitzvot.
Discuss the existence of different lists of Mitzvot.
Explain the concept of sanctity of life and its significance in Judaism.
Explain Pikuach Nefesh and its significance in personal, social and community life.
Discuss what kinds of life are sacred and whether Pikuach Nefesh extends to relieving suffering.
Explain the distinction and relationship between soul and body and its significance for views on life after death.
Define resurrection, judgement, Sheol, Gan Eden and Gehenna.
Explain the importance of beliefs about life after death and different ideas about bodily resurrection.
Compare Jewish views of judgement and its role in determining life after death.
Describe the structure of the synagogue service and the synagogue's design, artefacts and role in the community.
Explain worship in the home.
Explain the significance of the Ark, Bimah, lack of representation of G-d, Ner Tamid and Mikveh.
Explain the Torah readings, prayers and sermons, and the connection between synagogue and Temple.
Discuss length, structure, use of Hebrew, and differences between groups such as separating women and men.
Explain the role of prayer in Jewish worship, including the Amidah, and of private prayer.
Explain the three daily periods of prayer, spontaneous prayer, the Shema, Grace after meals, teaching children to pray and the direction faced.
Explain prayer for praise, confession, thanksgiving and supplication, and its link to the Mitzvot at home.
Discuss the purpose of prayer and differing views on attire for prayer.
Describe the Tenakh (Written Law), the Chumash and Sefer Torah.
Explain the Talmud (Oral Law) and how it relates to the Torah.
Explain the use of the Torah in the synagogue and the Tenakh in private worship, including Neviim and Ketuvim.
Explain how the Torah structures a Jew's daily life and compare views on the Torah and Talmud.
Explain the meaning, origins and significance of Shabbat.
Explain traditions and Mitzvot of Shabbat: preparation, candles, the meal, Havdalah and Kiddush.
Describe Shabbat services in the synagogue and home.
Discuss different understandings of what is prohibited, and attitudes to literal observance.
Explain the origins and importance of Rosh Hashanah: Teshuva, the Shofar, symbolic foods, the service and Tashlich.
Explain Yom Kippur: link to Rosh Hashanah, Book of Life, Kapparah, rules, fasting, services and Neilah.
Explain the Pilgrim Festivals, the Exodus story, chametz and the Seder meal.
Explain the origins and importance of Sukkot (sukkah and four species), Hanukkah, Pesach and Shavuot.
Discuss reconciling dates in different calendars and differing emphases between Jewish groups.
Explain the origin and nature of dietary laws and the meaning of Kosher and Terefah.
Explain the mitzvot on slaughter and eating of animals, poultry, fish, fruit and vegetables, and meat with milk.
Explain the impact of dietary laws on Jewish lifestyle.
Discuss pikuach nefesh and breaking kashrut, and preparation of food by non-Jews.
Explain the meaning of rites of passage.
Describe birth ceremonies: welcoming a baby girl, Brit Milah and the covenant with Abraham, circumcision, the father, Mohel and Sandek.
Describe Bar/Bat Mitzvah: preparation, the service, later preparations and Bat Chayil.
Describe Kiddushin and the wedding: Ketubah, Huppah, wine, ring, breaking the glass and blessings.
Describe burial rites: burial, tearing of clothes and Kaddish.
Compare attitudes to women's role in rites of passage and to Bat Mitzvah.
Describe the life of Buddha: early life, the Four Sights, defeat of Mara, Enlightenment and Nibbana.
Explain the importance of Buddha for Buddhists in the modern world.
Compare how different Buddhist groups emphasise the life of Buddha.
Explain the Dhamma as eternal law and Buddha's teachings and as one of the Three Jewels.
Explain dependent origination and its relationship to samsara.
Explain the Three Marks of Existence: dukkha, anicca and anatta, and their significance.
Explain the 12 links (nidanas) across three lifetimes.
Compare different Buddhist definitions of the Dhamma.
Explain the First Noble Truth that life is suffering (dukkha).
Distinguish dukkha-dukkha, viparinama-dukkha and sankhara-dukkha.
Discuss interconnections between forms of suffering and whether all sentient beings can be liberated.
Explain the cause of suffering: samudaya and craving (tanha).
Explain the three poisons or fires: Lobha, Dosa and Moha, and how they relate to suffering.
Discuss opposite qualities to the three poisons and different understandings of ignorance, attachment and aversion.
Explain the end of suffering and the meaning of nibbana (to extinguish).
Compare ways of understanding nibbana and Enlightenment.
Explain the cessation of craving and different views of the relationship between nibbana and rebirth.
Explain the elements of the Eightfold Path (magga), its importance and grouping.
Explain the Threefold Way: sila, samadhi and panna, and its importance.
Discuss the relationship between the Eightfold Path and Threefold Way, and ways of putting the path into practice.
Explain the five aggregates (khandas) in Theravada Buddhism and their link to anicca, anatta and dependent origination.
Explain the Mahayana concepts of sunyata, tathagatagarbha and buddha-nature.
Explain how these concepts relate to the Four Noble Truths and to Buddhist practice.
Define Arahant/Arhat, Bodhisattva and Buddha and their characteristics.
Describe the paths and stages by which these states are achieved.
Explain Buddhist attitudes to human destiny: Bodhisattva ideals, Buddhahood and Pure Land.
Discuss the distinction between an arhat and a buddha and their role for other beings.
Define kamma/karma, rebirth, compassion (karuna) and loving kindness (metta).
Explain the Five Precepts and Six Perfections and the role of ethical principles.
Explain the relationship between kamma and the Eightfold Path, samsara and nibbana, and between the path and ethical principles.
Discuss balancing compassion with wisdom and views on other perfections.

subtopics.title: Application of Buddhist principles in modern life

outcomes.text: Explain internalisation of virtue and skilful and unskilful action in relation to kamma and rebirth.
Explain the Middle Way for moral conduct and abstaining from immoral conduct.
Discuss applying ancient principles and Precepts to modern ethical issues.
Explain forms of worship: meditation, chanting, puja, mantra, malas and offerings.
Explain the significance of worship in the temple and the home and the purpose of devotional ritual.
Explain the relationship between devotional worship and ending dukkha, and the meaning of artefacts such as malas.
Describe the form, focus and aim of Samatha, metta bhavana, Vipassana, Zazen, mindfulness and visualisation meditation.
Explain the relationship between meditation and the Eightfold Path.
Explain the features and functions of temples, gompas and viharas, shrines, pilgrimage sites and retreats.
Describe events at significant places such as Bodh Gaya and the Deer Park at Sarnath.
Explain key artefacts and offerings, including images of the Buddha and mudras.
Explain the purpose and form of retreats and the importance of pilgrimage.
Explain the Sangha as one of the Three Jewels and the roles of monastic and lay sangha.
Describe the Ten Precepts observed by monks and nuns.
Discuss the ordination of women into the monastic sangha and differing rules in monasteries.
Explain the origins, stories and customs of Wesak or Hanamatsuri, Vassa, Uposatha days, Parinirvana day and Lama Tsong Khapa Day.
Explain the importance of marking parts of the Buddha's life and the purpose of Vassa and Uposatha days.
Explain the purpose and popularity of festivals not directly about the Buddha, and local cultural influence on festival practice.
Describe death and mourning rituals in Theravada communities, in Tibet and in Japan (Obon).
Explain Buddhist beliefs about death and rebirth, and the meaning of death rituals within kamma, rebirth and the six realms.
Explain the Tibetan Book of the Dead and Bardo, and the events and significance of Obon.
Explain death and the teaching on impermanence, and local cultural influence on mourning rituals.
Explain atman as the eternal self liberated from samsara.
Explain atman as identical with Brahman and as distinct from Brahman.
Compare Hindu understandings of atman, liberation (moksha), the atman-Brahman relationship and the approaches of different yogas.

subtopics.title: The cycle of birth, life and death

outcomes.text: Define samsara, maya, detachment and moksha and explain how they connect.
Explain the relationship between rebirth in samsara and karma.
Compare Hindu views on these concepts, including being jivan mukti (liberated while alive).
Explain karma and its role in Hindu life and rebirth, as causality and cosmic justice.
Explain jivan mukti and the relationship of karma with samsara.
Explain parabdha karma and kriyamana karma and the link to moral thinking.
Explain sakam and nishkam karma and their relation to rebirth and liberation.
Define maya, loka, devas and asuras and explain how lokas are divided.
Describe the heavenly realms of the Tri-Murti and their inhabitants, and rebirth into realms through karma.
Explain prakriti, purusha and the trigunas in the creation of the material world.
Explain the cycle of creation and destruction, the Trimurti and the Mahayuga.
Compare Hindu cosmology: cyclical universe, aum, mahayuga and the material world and maya.
Explain Brahman with attributes (Saguna) and without attributes (Nirguna) and how Brahman acts in the world.
Explain the Trimurti and Tridevi, Shakti and the relationship between male and female deities.
Explain Avatara as incarnation of deities and its significance in different traditions.
Explain Murti as the focus of worship and an expression of actual presence.
Explain Brahman as eternal, omnipresent, impersonal (nirguna) and as a personal deity in forms (saguna).
Explain Brahman as all-pervading and within the heart (antaryami), and as supreme person (Bhagavan or Ishvara).
Explain how different understandings of Brahman relate to liberation, and the importance of a personal deity.

subtopics.title: The four aims of human life (Purusharthas)

outcomes.text: Explain dharma and its role in Hindu life.
Explain the relationship of dharma to varna, ashrama, artha, karma and moksha.
Explain Sanatana dharma and the relationship of individual dharma to karma.
Compare Hindu understandings of the four aims and of varna.
Explain Hindu understanding of free will, suffering and virtue in relation to karma and samsara.
Explain the yamas: ahimsa, daya, dama and dana, and their relation to dharma.
Compare which virtues Hindu groups identify as core.
Explain the four margas: jnana, bhakti, karma and astanga/raja yoga, and their approaches and practices.
Explain the significance of Varnashramadharma for individuals and society.
Explain the relationship of these ways of living to karma and moksha.
Explain svadharma, sewa and dana as Hindu approaches to social concerns.
Compare emphases on ways of living, including following more than one yoga.
Explain havan or homa, puja, meditation, japa, bhajan or kirtan and darshan.
Explain the importance of temples, shrines, pilgrimage sites, outdoors, hills and rivers as sacred places.
Explain the role of gurus and sadhus/sadhvis and of sacred plants and animals.
Explain pilgrimage, sites such as Varanasi and the Ganges, and links to the yogas.
Explain darshan in relation to murti, holy people and holy places.
Explain the origins, deities, stories and customs of Holi, Navaratri, Diwali, Maha Shivaratri, Ganesh Chaturthi and Raksha Bandhan.
Explain why Ganesh Chaturthi is so widely celebrated.
Compare Hindu attitudes to festivals and their importance across branches.
Explain Hindu teachings on the environment and treatment of animals.
Explain Hinduism and social issues: social responsibility, inclusion and women's rights.
Describe how teachings are put into practice through projects: Assisi Declarations 1986, goshallas and the Ahimsa Foundation for cattle, Sewa International.

units.title: Christianity: Religion, philosophy and ethics in the modern world

outcomes.text: Explain Christian attitudes to the role and purpose of the family, and to the importance and purposes of marriage.
Explain the beliefs and teachings reflected in a Christian marriage ceremony and why practice differs.
Explain Christian views on same-sex marriage, civil partnership, pre-marital sex, cohabitation, celibacy and contraception.
Evaluate the ethics of divorce, annulment and remarriage, with justifications from different denominations.
Explain Christian beliefs about the roles of men and women in family relationships and Christian communities.
Explain Christian views on the religious upbringing of children.
Discuss equality of men and women, freedom of choice and its restrictions, and duty to family and community.
Explain Christian teachings and beliefs about equality and the influence of culture on views.
Explain the importance of equality for individuals, communities and society.
Explain Christian attitudes to prejudice and discrimination based on gender, and the ideas of embedded inequalities.
Explain different Christian beliefs about what God is like and God's relationship with the world and humanity.
Explain Christian understandings of God as good and what goodness means in God's actions.
Explain Christian views on the problem of evil and the relationship between God and human suffering.
Explain arguments for God's existence: design (teleological), first cause (cosmological), moral argument and awe and wonder.
Explain the world as formed for humanity, including the Anthropic principle, and the world and moral consequence, soul-making and judgement.
Evaluate the value and importance of arguments for God's existence.
Explain ways Christians believe God is revealed: inspirational people, scripture, Jesus Christ, Christian history, God acting in the world, conscience and miracles.
Explain forms of religious experience: conversion, mystical, charismatic and ecstatic, visions, worship and sacraments.
Explain how Christian teachings on violence are applied by individuals and communities, and their role in society.
Explain the relationship between religion, politics and terrorism in the 21st century and Christian attitudes to terrorism.
Explain Just War Theory and the concept of Holy War, and religious attitudes to behaviour in war.
Compare Christian attitudes to conventional, technological (drones) and nuclear warfare.
Explain pacifism: absolute and conditional, and Christian attitudes to it.
Describe how individuals, communities and society work for peace: Gandhi, Martin Luther King, Desmond Tutu and CCND.
Discuss using violence to achieve peace, non-violent action and whether peace-making should be Christians' most important activity.
Explain forgiveness and reconciliation and the impact of teachings on justice, forgiveness and reconciliation.
Discuss whether forgiveness is possible or desirable, using examples such as the South African Truth and Reconciliation Commission.
Explain justice and injustice, the relationship between peace and a just society, and how Christians work for social justice.

Explain areas of disagreement between Christianity and non-religious views and their significance.
